def.brief:
Add the regression tests for amendment G9 to test_red_gate.py (a new TestCase class, methods named test_G9_...), changing nothing else in that file. Simulate the Windows constraint behaviourally: replace subprocess.Popen (unittest.mock.patch("subprocess.Popen", ...)) with a subclass whose __init__ raises AssertionError("pass_fds not supported on Windows.") when given a non-empty pass_fds and otherwise behaves as Popen, then call worker.unittest_red on real fixture files in a temporary directory. A call that raises must fail the test by an assertion (catch BaseException around the call and self.fail with what was raised), never by an error of the test itself. Also show that nothing is left inside the target but __pycache__. Import the candidate from this directory; no model, host or network calls; remove temporary directories. Run once: the new tests must fail now by assertions only (zero errors) and every earlier test in the file must still pass. Do not change test_hacheong.py or any other file.

CONTRACT B, amendment G9 (found by the session's review of b-redgate-build, which hands REPORT back through os.pipe() and subprocess pass_fds). CPython refuses a non-empty pass_fds on Windows with `assert not pass_fds, "pass_fds not supported on Windows."` — an AssertionError that unittest_red does not catch, so validate() and the worker would crash and write no answer there. G1-G8 stand unchanged.

G9. unittest_red needs no file descriptor passed to the harness process and never raises: under a subprocess whose Popen refuses any non-empty pass_fds with AssertionError("pass_fds not supported on Windows.") — as CPython does on Windows — it gives the same verdicts as on POSIX: "red" for a TestCase whose body calls self.fail, "green" for an all-passing TestCase, "unverified" for a file importing a missing module at the top, and "unverified" for a test that calls os._exit(0) (no report). Its channel still is not unittest's printed output and leaves nothing inside target (a scratch file, if any, lives outside target and is removed afterwards). On this POSIX machine every G1-G8 verdict stays as it is.

non-claims: no check decides this task; done means the agent said so

(provider) "a scratch file, if any, lives outside target and is removed afterwards" is only checked for scratch files made through tempfile or under TMPDIR/TEMP/TMP. Those are pointed at a fresh directory that must be empty afterwards. A scratch file written to some other hard-coded place outside target would not be seen.

(provider) "as CPython does on Windows" is simulated on POSIX by a Popen that refuses a non-empty pass_fds. Other Windows differences (handle inheritance, msvcrt, path and signal behaviour) cannot be seen from here.

(provider) The Windows simulation only applies if unittest_red reaches Popen through the subprocess module attribute. Each test asserts that the patched Popen was actually used, so a harness started some other way (os.spawn*, os.posix_spawn, a Popen reference saved before the patch) fails the test rather than slipping past it.
(provider) "On this POSIX machine every G1-G8 verdict stays as it is" is decided by the existing G1-G8 tests in the same file, not by a new G9 test. All of them pass now.

response.summary: I added a new class, G9NoPassFds, to test_red_gate.py with 7 test_G9_* tests. Nothing else in that file changed (91 lines added), and no other file was touched. Each test swaps subprocess.Popen, using mock.patch("subprocess.Popen", ...), for a subclass of the real Popen that raises AssertionError("pass_fds not supported on Windows.") whenever pass_fds is non-empty. It then calls worker.unittest_red on real fixture files in temporary directories that get removed afterwards. Any exception from the call is caught as BaseException and turned into self.fail, so a crash shows up as a test failure, not a test error. Each test also checks that the harness really started through the patched Popen, so code that dodges the patch can't pass. I ran `python3 -m unittest test_red_gate.py` once: 72 tests ran, the 7 new G9 tests failed by assertion (all with 'unittest_red raised AssertionError: pass_fds not supported on Windows.'), there were 0 errors, and all 65 earlier tests passed.
